note: Malta: EEA and Swiss nationals live and work freely (the eea list). A non-EU national needs a residence permit to be employed: the Single Permit for six months or more, or for less a residence permit on a Jobsplus employment licence for that period (Identità, Expatriates Unit). Identità names no days a performer may work without either, so none are modelled.

sources.title: Identità, Expatriates Unit: Non-EU Nationals – Employment Related Permits
sources.said: Non-EU Nationals require a residence permit to be employed in Malta. The first step in qualifying for employment is to have an employment offer from an employer in Malta.

sources.title: Identità, Expatriates Unit: Non-EU Nationals – Employment Under Six Months
sources.said: A third-country national employed for less than six months may apply for a residence permit upon the presentation of a valid employment license issued for that period from Jobsplus. ... In case the third-country national wishes to reside and work in Malta for six months or more, a Single Work Permit is required.
